title: Israeli Attacks Force Families to Flee in Southern Syria — Turkey Says It's Against the Law
summary:
Late Sunday night, families in the Syrian village of Abdin had to grab their kids and run. Israeli soldiers had moved into the area, and when villagers tried to block them, the soldiers fired shells that landed dangerously close to homes. "Shells fell near the houses," said Mahmoud Mouaffak, a village leader. Everyone fled to nearby villages in the dark.

By Monday morning, the Israeli forces had pulled back, and people started returning. One man was seen checking an unexploded shell right next to his house — imagine finding that in your yard!

This is part of a bigger pattern. Since Syria's old government fell in late 2024, Israel has been sending troops deeper into southern Syria. They've even moved into a buffer zone near the Golan Heights, an area Israel has occupied since 1967. A group that tracks Israeli activity says there were nearly 300 operations or violations in June alone — that's about 10 every day!

Israel says it's going after "armed terrorists," but they didn't say how many or show any evidence. Meanwhile, Israel's defense minister said last week that Israeli troops plan to stay in parts of Syria "for an indefinite period" — just like they do in Lebanon and Gaza.

Turkey, which is friendly with Syria's new government, strongly condemned the attacks. Turkey's foreign ministry said the attacks "trample on the lives and property of the Syrian people" and are a "flagrant violation of international law." Syria's government also called the attacks a violation of its sovereignty.

For Syrian families still recovering from 13 years of war, these new attacks make life even harder and scarier.
why_it_matters: When soldiers cross into another country's land and shoot near homes, innocent kids and families get hurt, and it's important that countries follow rules that protect people during conflicts.

background_read: Syria has been through a terrible civil war that started in 2011. In late 2024, its old government fell, and a new group took over the country.
The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau that Israel captured from Syria during the 1967 war. Since then, Israel has occupied the area, and a buffer zone keeps Israeli and Syrian forces apart.
Turkey, a powerful neighbor that shares a border with Syria, supports the new Syrian government and has spoken out strongly against the Israeli attacks.
Article_Structure: WHO: Israeli soldiers and Syrian villagers from Abdin.
WHAT: Israeli forces entered the village, shelled near homes, causing families to flee in the dark. By morning, the soldiers pulled back.
WHERE: Abdin village in southern Syria, near the Golan Heights buffer zone.
WHY: Israel says it targets armed terrorists, but Turkey and Syria say the attacks are illegal and harm innocent people.

perspectives.description: Israel argues that it is targeting 'armed terrorists' who might attack its own people, so entering Syrian territory is needed for security.
Turkey and the Syrian government say these attacks violate international law and harm civilians, and that Israel should not be allowed to stay on Syrian land.
Analysts note that Israel has increased its military operations in Syria since the government changed, raising fears that the region could become more unstable.
